parts.heading: What a session is
parts.text: Each session is a visit to one artist's studio. We sit down for an interview, photograph the space and the work in progress, and make a short film of the artist at work.

parts.heading: Our rule on interviews
parts.text: Every conversation we publish is a real one. An interview appears here only after it has taken place and the artist has approved the transcript. We do not write imagined or reconstructed dialogue.

paras: Through reported profiles, studio notes and cultural essays, we look at the ideas, experiences and creative decisions behind today's artistic practices.

parts.heading: What we publish
parts.text: Features and reported essays. Artist stories. Notes from the studio on materials and working methods. Writing on culture and exhibitions. And The Studio Sessions, our series of interviews, photographs and short films.

parts.heading: How we work
parts.text: We publish an interview only when it has really taken place and the transcript has been approved by the person interviewed. Until then, a piece is a feature or a reported essay and is described as one.

parts.heading: How we report
parts.text: Every feature lists its sources at the foot of the page, so you can check what we have said. We write in our own words and do not invent quotations. Where published accounts disagree, we say so and do not pick a side without evidence.

parts.heading: Corrections
parts.text: If we have something wrong, tell us and we will put it right on the page.

privacy.title: Privacy | The Art Correspondent
privacy.description: What The Art Correspondent does with information about readers and the people who write to us.

paras: This page explains what happens to information about you when you use The Art Correspondent. The short version: there is no advertising, visitor statistics (Google Analytics) run only if you press Accept, and the only personal details we keep are the ones you send us yourself.

parts.heading: Who is responsible
parts.text:
The Art Correspondent is published by Artiscope Ltd, which is responsible for personal information collected through this site. For anything on this page, write to [info@artiscope.co.uk](mailto:info@artiscope.co.uk?subject=Privacy).

Artiscope Ltd is registered in England and Wales, company number 16048878.

parts.heading: If you use the contact form
parts.text:
The [contact form](../contact/) sends us your name, your email address, any topic you pick, and your message, with the time it was sent and which of our sites it came from. We use them to read your message and reply. We do not add you to a mailing list and we do not pass your details to anyone else.

The law calls our reason for keeping them legitimate interests: you have written to us, and we need your message and address to answer you.

The messages are kept for us by Supabase, a database service, on servers in Ireland. Supabase also keeps short-lived technical records of each request so it can run and secure its service. Only the Artiscope team can read the messages.

We delete form messages 12 months after our last reply, sooner if you ask. The only exception is a message we need to keep to deal with a complaint or a legal claim, and then only for as long as that takes.

parts.heading: If you email us or ask to join a list
parts.text:
If you email us, we see your address and whatever you write, and use them to reply.

The subscribe boxes on our sites do not send anything themselves. They open your own email app with a message to us. If you send it, we keep your name and email address in our email inbox and use them only to send you what you asked for. That rests on your consent, and you can withdraw it at any time by writing to us. We keep your address until you leave the list.

parts.heading: What happens when a page loads
parts.text:
Whenever your browser fetches a web page, the server it asks sees some technical details, such as your IP address, your browser and the page you wanted. These services are involved here:

[GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement) hosts the site, and GitHub keeps server records to run and protect its service.

[Google Fonts](https://policies.google.com/privacy) supplies the typefaces, so your browser asks Google's servers for them.

[Google Analytics](https://policies.google.com/privacy) counts visits and the pages read, only if you press Accept on the statistics bar. This is based on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

[Supabase](https://supabase.com/privacy) receives anything you send through the contact form, as described above.

We use them because a website needs them to work, which again counts as legitimate interests. GitHub and Google are based in the United States, so some of these details may be handled there. Each company's privacy policy explains how it looks after them.

parts.heading: Cookies and your browser
parts.text:
The site contains no advertising code. On your first visit a small bar asks whether we may count your visit. Only if you press Accept does the site load Google Analytics, which sets cookies whose names start with _ga (kept for up to two years) to tell one visit from another. We use what it shows only to see which pages are read and how visitors find us. Google's advertising features are switched off, and if your browser sends a Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control signal, we do not ask and do not count your visit. Your answer is kept in your own browser, and you can [change your statistics choice](#cookie-settings) at any time.

The site keeps a small note in your own browser for the length of your visit when you have already seen a pop-up, so it does not keep coming back. These notes stay on your device and are never sent to us. Closing the tab clears the short-lived ones, and you can clear the rest in your browser settings at any time.

parts.heading: Links to other sites
parts.text: Our pages link to their sources. Those sites have their own privacy policies, and what happens there is up to them.

parts.heading: Your rights
parts.text:
You can ask us for a copy of the personal information we hold about you, and ask us to correct it, delete it or limit how we use it. Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time.

You also have the right to object to us using your information where we rely on legitimate interests. If you object, we will stop unless we have a strong reason to carry on that outweighs yours.

To use any of these rights, write to [info@artiscope.co.uk](mailto:info@artiscope.co.uk?subject=My%20information). We will answer within one month. We do not sell your information and we do not make automated decisions about you.

parts.heading: If you are unhappy
parts.text:
Please tell us first, at [info@artiscope.co.uk](mailto:info@artiscope.co.uk?subject=Data%20protection%20complaint). We will acknowledge your complaint within 30 days, look into it and tell you what we found.

You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office, the UK's data protection regulator, at [ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint](https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/) or on 0303 123 1113.

parts.heading: Changes to this page
parts.text: If we change how we handle information, we will update this page. The date at the top shows when it last changed.

paras: These terms cover your use of The Art Correspondent. By using the site you accept them, so please read them. They are short.

parts.heading: Who we are
parts.text: The Art Correspondent is published by Artiscope Ltd, registered in England and Wales, company number 16048878. You can reach us at [info@artiscope.co.uk](mailto:info@artiscope.co.uk).

parts.heading: What our pages are for
parts.text: Our articles are general information. They are not financial, legal, tax or investment advice, and nothing here is a valuation. An auction result is a past price and does not tell you what a work will fetch next time. Before you buy, sell or insure a work of art, take advice from someone who knows your circumstances.

parts.heading: Accuracy
parts.text: We take every fact and figure from a published source and show where it came from. Sources can be wrong, and things change after we write about them. If you spot a mistake, please [tell us](../contact/) and we will look into it.

parts.heading: Using our content
parts.text:
The writing on The Art Correspondent belongs to Artiscope Ltd. You are welcome to quote short passages, as long as you name The Art Correspondent and link to the page. Please ask us before copying whole articles or republishing them anywhere else.

Pictures belong to the artists and photographers named with them. Some are used under a licence, such as Creative Commons, and where that is so the licence is named in the credit. Check it before you reuse a picture. A licence for a photograph of an artwork covers the photograph, not the artwork, which may still be protected by the artist's copyright.

Names of artists, galleries, auction houses and other businesses belong to their owners. Mentioning them does not mean they endorse us or are connected with us.

parts.heading: Writing to us
parts.text: Please do not send us anything unlawful, or anything confidential you would not want us to keep. If you send a correction, we may use it to fix the page, without naming you unless you agree. [Our privacy page](../privacy/) explains what happens to your message.

parts.heading: Links to other sites
parts.text: We link to our sources so you can check them. We do not run those sites and are not responsible for what they publish. A link is not an endorsement.

parts.heading: Our responsibility
parts.text:
We work hard to keep the site accurate and available, but we provide it as it is, and we cannot promise it will always be free of mistakes or interruptions. As far as the law allows, we are not responsible for any loss caused by relying on it.

Nothing in these terms limits any responsibility that cannot be limited by law, such as for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud.

parts.heading: Law
